lab_title: VSEPR Theory: Exploring Molecular Geometry in 3D
top_level_objectives: Explain the fundamental postulate of VSEPR theory: minimizing electron-domain repulsion.
Distinguish between electron-domain geometry and molecular shape.
Identify the five fundamental molecular geometries based on electron count.
Analyze how lone pairs distort ideal bond angles in molecules like water and ammonia.
Predict molecular shapes for common covalent compounds using VSEPR theory.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the core concept of electron domain repulsion.
key_visuals: A central atom with two floating, repulsive electron-cloud spheres.
student_actions: Use a slider to add electron domains to a central atom.
Observe how the spheres automatically space themselves out to minimize overlap.

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize the five fundamental electron-domain geometries.
key_visuals: A selection menu for geometries (Linear to Octahedral).
3D skeletal models showing positions of electron domains.
student_actions: Select different geometries to project the skeletal arrangements into their physical space.
Rotate the molecules to understand the spatial distribution of the domains.

scenes.brief_purpose: Differentiate between electron geometry and molecular geometry using lone pairs.
key_visuals: A toggle switch for 'Show Lone Pairs'.
Visual indicator showing lone pairs occupying 'larger' space than bonding pairs.
student_actions: Swap bonding pairs for lone pairs in a tetrahedral arrangement.
Observe the structural change from tetrahedral to trigonal pyramidal, then to bent.

scenes.brief_purpose: Observe bond angle deviation due to lone pair pressure.
key_visuals: Comparative side-by-side view of Methane (ideal) and Water (distorted).
Measurements showing the reduction of bond angles.
student_actions: Compare the H-C-H angle of methane to the H-O-H angle of water.
Drag a slider to simulate increased 'pressure' from lone pairs to see the angles shift.

scenes.brief_purpose: Test understanding by matching real molecules to their geometries.
key_visuals: A 'Molecule Lab' table with 3D renderings of PF5, SF6, and XeF4.
An interactive assessment prompt asking to label the shapes.
student_actions: Pick up virtual molecular models (e.g., SF6).
Identify the central atom and electron-domain geometry for each sample to verify the VSEPR prediction.
